recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements—the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recGibxmAutKKDKtO.Bio: Dr. Moshe Daniel Block is a naturopathic doctor who works on mind-body healing of collective trauma; on InnerVerse he discussed Jewish identity, the victim/perpetrator dynamic, scapegoat archetypes, and generational trauma.
recGibxmAutKKDKtO.Name: Dr. Moshe Daniel Block

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Following the thread until the belief shows", "body": "Block describes his practice as one where the questions do the work: a client repeats certain words, the words carry themes, and a complaint about a boss who never listens deepens into feeling small, which only becomes a theme once it turns up again with a boyfriend. Garton works from the other end, dowsing a biofield for static and tracing a veterinarian's recurring septic trouble back to a babysitter's house that smelled wrong. Both treat the pattern as the trail, and Block says he will not start without a focused issue, real permission, and the client's own money on the table."}, {"title": "Fire, taste and the limits of nutrition", "body": "A long middle stretch runs through traditional Chinese medicine as Block understands it, where the pathogens are damp, cold and wind rather than microbes, where nourishment is credited to the five tastes rather than to nutrients, and where defensive chi is said to withdraw into the body around eleven at night. He recounts a pharmaceutical rep in Montreal whose colitis symptoms disappeared on junk food weekends with old friends and returned on a pristine diet, and argues from that case that mental and emotional work can outrank food. Garton says he avoids diet debates because the evidence contradicts itself."}, {"title": "The half truth of staying positive", "body": "Block keeps returning to the hermetic axiom that all truths are half truths, and turns it on positivity: refusing to look at the negative is still a relationship with it, and the loudly sunny person often has something raging underneath. Garton borrows Michael Tsarion's phrase, smiling depressives, and reads the profile picture grin as a primate submission display. Both treat hard lines as armour, the wall someone strains to hold up while an equal pressure builds on the far side, and Garton offers accepting as protecting in place of cutting the difficult people out of your life."}, {"title": "Four worlds and one life force", "body": "Working from a diagram in his book, Block lays out soul, mind, emotion and body as nested worlds and maps them onto the Kabbalistic Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah, onto Shen, Qi and Jing, and onto the yogic koshas down to the food body. Illness, he argues, begins as a false premise in the mind, blocks Shen, then chi, then blood. Garton adds his own framing that life force is a fractal singularity, intact whatever vessel holds it, which is how he accounts for tuning fork sessions that seem to land on clients in another country entirely."}, {"title": "Letters, cycles and the end of days", "body": "The last stretch goes deep into Hebrew. Block treats it as an initiatic script rather than street language, unpacks the three mother letters shin, mem and aleph as fire, water and the steam bearing air between them, and reads bereshit as the end already sitting inside the beginning, an ouroboros. Garton counters the standard Phoenician ox head reading of aleph with a bellows, a bag of breath. From there they move to prophecy, the days of Noah and the Nephilim, and Block's view that end times mark a demarcation and a mass awakening rather than a finish."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: As promised after his last InnerVerse appearance, Dr. Moshe Daniel Block is back to Vibe Rant on some of the excellent mind-body-earth synergy that emerge from his diverse knowledge sets. We'll talk about the Kabbalah of holistic health and alignment of natural electromagnetic forces for personal development and gardening.
